title: API 570 Training in Los Angeles: Piping Inspector Exam Prep
description: API 570 exam prep online for Los Angeles piping inspectors: refinery and harbour piping, CUI in salt air, injection points, dead legs. Instructor Q&A.
h1: API 570 Training in Los Angeles: Self-Paced Exam Prep for Refinery, Terminal and Dock Piping Inspectors
html:
API 570 exam prep for piping inspectors from El Segundo to the harbour

In the Los Angeles basin a piping inspector's work rarely stops at one fence. Unit piping inside the South Bay refineries joins interconnecting lines between sites, product pipelines to terminals, hydrogen lines from merchant plants and dock lines running out over the water at the Port of Los Angeles and the Port of Long Beach. API 570 is the certification most owners look for in the people who plan and carry out inspection of that piping.

There is no Atlantis classroom in Los Angeles. The Atlantis API 570 course is online and self-paced, with instructor Q&A, so you can work through ASME B31.3, API 570 and RP 574 between shifts and send questions whenever a clause or calculation stops you. API sets the eligibility rules, administers the exam at Prometric test centres and grants the certification. Atlantis is not an API-approved provider, and nothing in the course replaces the application you make to API.

A piping network that crosses property lines

The pieces of this refining centre are tightly linked to one another. Some examples, from public sources:

  • Marathon's Los Angeles refinery combines plants in Carson and Wilmington, which the California Energy Commission says have reported as a single refinery since 2019. Operating two plants as one usually means intermediate and product lines between the sites, which bring road crossings and buried sections into a piping inspector's scope.
  • Phillips 66's Los Angeles refinery, which stopped refining in October 2025 according to EIA, was built the same way: crude was processed at the Carson site, and the pipeline-linked Wilmington site upgraded intermediates into finished products.
  • Kinder Morgan's Watson Station gathers products from the area's refineries and third-party terminals and feeds pipelines towards Colton, San Diego, Phoenix and, through the Calnev line, Las Vegas. Kinder Morgan's Carson terminal connects to Watson Station through Sepulveda Junction and receives ships at Berth 118.
  • Hydrogen lines. Air Products produces hydrogen in Wilmington and Carson and distributes it by pipeline; a project the City of Carson approved in 2020 would repurpose about 11.5 miles of existing pipe to carry hydrogen to a refinery in Paramount.

Inside the refineries, the piping follows the process: crude and vacuum units, delayed cokers and fluid catalytic crackers at all four of the large plants that EIA lists, catalytic hydrocrackers at three of them, plus alkylation and sulfur recovery, which EIA also lists at all four, and the amine and sour water systems that go with them. That mix gives an API 570 candidate from here practical experience of most RP 571 mechanisms on the exam list.

Where API 570 stops and pipeline regulation starts

Because so much pipe here leaves one property and enters another, it pays to know where the code ends. API 570 is written for in-service process piping in refineries, chemical plants and similar facilities. Pipelines that carry hazardous liquids between facilities are regulated under 49 CFR Part 195 instead: PHMSA has exclusive federal authority over interstate lines, such as those that cross into Arizona and Nevada, while California's Office of the State Fire Marshal has authority over intrastate hazardous liquid pipelines in the state.

The boundary is usually a valve, a flange or a scraper trap, and it is written into the owner's procedures rather than guessed in the field. The exam does not test 49 CFR 195, but a candidate who has worked at a terminal or pump station should expect questions that rely on understanding API 570's own scope. The page on the API 570 and pipeline code boundary sets out the usual dividing lines.

Dock lines and MOTEMS

Marine oil terminals in California follow the Marine Oil Terminal Engineering and Maintenance Standards, known as MOTEMS, which are part of the California Building Code as Chapter 31F and are enforced by the State Lands Commission. MOTEMS covers structures, mooring, fire protection, mechanical and electrical systems and pipelines on the wharf. Terminal operators complete audits and inspections on a recurring schedule, which the Commission describes as typically every four years, and they must inspect after significant events such as earthquakes, storms or fires. Changes to piping or pipeline components need a MOTEMS-compliant review before they go into use.

The Port of Los Angeles lists liquid bulk terminals operated by Kinder Morgan, PBF Energy, Phillips 66, Valero and Vopak, among others, and Long Beach has its own marine oil terminals. Dock piping meets damage that unit piping rarely sees in the same combination:

  • Atmospheric corrosion in salt air and splash, worst where coatings are damaged or water collects.
  • Corrosion at pipe supports and saddles, where the contact point stays wet and hides the metal loss.
  • Soil-to-air interfaces where lines leave the wharf and go underground towards the tank farm.
  • Movement and loading from vessel operations and, here, from earthquakes, which is why flexible connections and supports get attention after any strong event.

RP 574 discusses supports, soil-to-air interfaces and atmospheric corrosion, all examined in the API 570 Body of Knowledge, so a dock inspector from Wilmington or Long Beach recognises the material quickly.

Corrosion under insulation in a dry city with a damp coastline

Inland Los Angeles is dry for much of the year, which leads some newcomers to underrate CUI. The refineries and terminals, though, sit near the coast in marine air, and insulation gets wet from fog, rain, wash-down water, deluge testing and leaking steam tracing. API RP 571 puts the most susceptible range for carbon steel at roughly 10°F to 350°F, and for external chloride cracking of insulated austenitic stainless steel at roughly 140°F to 400°F. Lines that cycle through those ranges, or sit idle at ambient temperature, are prime candidates.

For the exam, know which locations RP 574 and API 570 single out: penetrations and terminations of insulation, low points, damaged jacketing, vertical runs where water tracks down, and piping in intermittent service. Know too that external visual inspection and CUI inspection have their own place in the inspection plan, separate from thickness readings at CMLs. For practice, see CUI in API 570 and API 510 inspection plans and the API RP 583 explainer.

Injection points in South Bay process units, with a worked circuit

Every large refinery here injects something into its piping: neutralizer and wash water into crude unit overheads, wash water upstream of hydroprocessing effluent air coolers, corrosion inhibitors and antifoulants at many other points. API 570 treats each injection point as its own circuit, because the zone just downstream is where corrosion concentrates. Injection points carry a three-year maximum thickness interval in API 570's interval table, shorter than the general class limits.

The circuit's length is a classic exam calculation. API 570 recommends an upstream limit at the greater of 12 in. or three pipe diameters before the injection point, and a downstream limit at the second change in flow direction past the injection point or 25 ft beyond the first change, whichever is less. Practise with these figures, which describe no real line:

  1. An NPS 8 line has an outside diameter of 8.625 in., so three diameters is 25.9 in. That beats 12 in., so the upstream limit is 25.9 in. before the injection point.
  2. The first elbow downstream is 10 ft from the injection point and the second is 40 ft from it.
  3. Twenty-five feet beyond the first change puts one candidate limit at 35 ft. The second change in direction is at 40 ft. The lesser of the two is 35 ft.
  4. So the injection point circuit runs from 25.9 in. upstream to 35 ft downstream, and CMLs are placed through that length, including at the elbows and the pipe opposite the injection nozzle.

Questions also ask what to examine at the next outage: the injection nozzle or quill itself, and the zone where the injected fluid meets the hot hydrocarbon. See injection point inspection under API 570 for more.

Dead legs left behind by closures and reroutes

Shutdowns and conversions create dead legs. When a unit stops, a refinery changes crude supply or a terminal reroutes product, branches that once flowed can sit full and stagnant, and corrosion in a dead leg can run much faster than in the active line it hangs from. API 570 expects inspectors to identify dead legs, to inspect both the stagnant end and the junction with the active line, and to consider removing branches that no longer serve a purpose.

The same events matter beyond piping rules. Under Cal/OSHA's refinery process safety standard, title 8 section 5189.1, a major change on a process where a damage mechanism exists triggers a review of the damage mechanism assessment before the change is approved. That is why piping inspectors at Los Angeles refineries are often asked to revisit CML locations and rates after a feed change, not just at the next scheduled interval. The dead leg inspection page goes further.

Routes into API 570 for Los Angeles workers

API requires piping experience gained in the last 10 years while employed by, or under contract with, an authorized inspection agency. With an engineering or technology degree, one year supervising or performing piping inspection is enough; a two-year degree or certificate needs two years of piping experience in design, fabrication, repair, operation or inspection, a high school diploma three, and no formal education five or more, each including at least a year of inspection. The API 570 certification requirements page explains the detail. Common starting points in the basin:

  • Pipe welders and fitters. Cerritos College in Norwalk offers pipe welding and process pipe welding certificates. Repair and fabrication years count as piping experience, but you still need a year performing or supervising inspection.
  • UT thickness technicians who take CML readings for refinery inspection departments and contractors, often the quickest route because the inspection year builds as they work.
  • Terminal operators and maintenance technicians at the harbour, who know the dock lines and manifolds but need inspection duties added to their role.
  • Holders of API 510, who often add API 570 because owners like one inspector covering vessels and the piping between them.

Studying API 570 on a South Bay schedule

The API 570 open-book half is mostly a search through ASME B31.3 and ASME B16.5, and the PDFs on the test-centre screen are plain, without your tabs or highlighting. Practise in the same conditions: open the code PDF, read the question, decide which document holds the answer, then find it. The course's practice papers copy the closed-book and open-book split, and the instructor can show where a paragraph sits when your search keeps missing it.

Build the B31.3 calculations into the closed-book part of your preparation as well, because corrosion rate, remaining life and interval questions can appear before lunch, without the code. For extra questions, use the API 570 practice questions and the API 570 code explainer.

Sponsoring a piping inspection group

Refinery inspection departments, terminal operators at the harbour and the contractors that serve both can enrol several API 570 candidates together, or a mix of API 570 and API 653 candidates where a team covers tanks as well. Each person studies at their own pace with the instructor, and fees are quoted on request. Prometric lists test centres in and around Los Angeles; once API accepts each application, the candidate books their own seat within the exam window.

faq.q: Does API 570 cover the pipelines that leave Watson Station?
faq.a: Generally not. Pipelines that move hazardous liquids between facilities fall under 49 CFR Part 195, with PHMSA overseeing interstate lines and the California Office of the State Fire Marshal overseeing intrastate ones. API 570 covers process piping inside the facility. Where exactly one ends and the other begins is set in the owner's procedures, usually at a valve, flange or scraper trap, so ask before you inspect.

faq.q: Are dock lines at the Port of Los Angeles API 570 piping?
faq.a: Marine oil terminal piping in California is covered by MOTEMS, Chapter 31F of the California Building Code, which the State Lands Commission enforces through audits and inspections. Many terminal owners also manage that piping within an API 570-style inspection programme. The two do not conflict, but MOTEMS has its own requirements and post-event inspections, so a dock inspector should know both.

faq.q: Is corrosion under insulation a real problem in a climate as dry as Los Angeles?
faq.a: Yes, at the coastal sites where most of the refineries and terminals are. Marine air, fog, rain, wash-down water and leaking steam tracing all wet insulation, and lines that run in the susceptible temperature range or cycle in and out of service are the most at risk. The exam tests where CUI is likely and how it fits into the inspection plan, not the weather in any city.

faq.q: How do I work out an injection point circuit on the API 570 exam?
faq.a: Take the upstream limit as the greater of 12 in. or three pipe diameters before the injection point. Take the downstream limit as the second change in flow direction past the injection point or 25 ft beyond the first change, whichever is less. Then place CMLs through that length. Practise with real pipe outside diameters, because nominal size alone gives the wrong three-diameter distance.

faq.q: Can a pipe welder who trained at Cerritos College qualify for API 570?
faq.a: Possibly. Welding and fabrication years count as piping experience, but every route includes at least one year spent supervising or performing piping inspection, and the total years depend on your education. A high school diploma means three years of experience in all, for example. Many welders get there by moving into QA/QC or welding inspection roles; the AWS CWI route is described on the CWI page for Los Angeles.

faq.q: Should a Los Angeles inspector take API 510 or API 570 first?
faq.a: Take the one that matches the equipment you inspect now, because your experience record has to support the application. Refinery inspectors who split their time often sit both, usually in successive windows. The comparison on API 510 versus API 570 sets out how the codes and exams differ, and the course structure lets you prepare for the second while the first is still fresh.

faq.q: Where do Los Angeles candidates take the API 570 exam?
faq.a: In person at a Prometric test centre. Prometric lists test centres in and around Los Angeles, and you choose one when you schedule after API approves your application. The day runs about 7.5 hours with a closed-book part, a lunch break and an open-book part on screen. See the API exam schedule for windows and deadlines.
